facts.statement: The genus Polonosuchus was formally described by Brusatte and colleagues in 2009.
facts.quote: authority: Brusatte et al., 2009

facts.statement: The species was originally described in 2005 by Tomasz Sulej under the name Teratosaurus silesiacus.
facts.quote: It was described as Teratosaurus silesiacus in 2005 by Tomasz Sulej

facts.statement: Polonosuchus lived during the Carnian age of the Late Triassic in Poland.
facts.quote: Polonosuchus is a genus of rauisuchid known from the late Triassic (Carnian age) of Poland

facts.statement: Polonosuchus was a predator characterized by a large head containing long, sharp teeth.
facts.quote: It was a predator equipped with a large head of long sharp teeth

facts.statement: Its legs were positioned almost directly beneath its body, suggesting it was a fast and powerful runner.
facts.quote: The legs were placed almost underneath the body, unlike most reptiles, which would have made it quite fast and a powerful runner

facts.statement: Polonosuchus shared a similar appearance and the ecological niche of an apex predator with the North American genus Postosuchus.
facts.quote: The appearance was very similar to that of the more known Postosuchus, of North America, and shared with the latter the ecological niche of the apex predator

facts.statement: The only known specimen of Polonosuchus is a fragmentary holotype.
facts.quote: The holotype, and only known specimen, is fragmentary

facts.statement: The fossil preserves various skull bones including the maxillae, premaxillae, nasals, and several jaw and palate elements.
facts.quote: From the skull are preserved both maxillae, premaxillae, nasals, prefrontals, palatines and quadrates, the left jugal, the right pterygoid, quadratojugal, surangular, articular, squamosal and lacrimal, and fragments of the dentary

facts.statement: The specimen includes the first three neck vertebrae, nine tail vertebrae, some tail scutes, and fragments of neck ribs.
facts.quote: There are also the first three cervical vertebrae, nine caudal vertebrae, some caudal scutes and fragments of cervical ribs

facts.statement: At least eleven tooth sockets were present in the maxillae, though the total number is uncertain due to damage.
facts.quote: At least eleven dental alveoli were present, although the total is not certain as both maxillae are broken off at the posterior ends

facts.statement: Evidence of replacement teeth suggests Polonosuchus was likely a polyphyodont, continuously replacing its teeth throughout life.
facts.quote: Small replacement teeth are visible above some of the alveoli, indicating it was probably a polyphyodont

facts.statement: The prefrontal bones were large triangular plates that overhung the eye sockets and had rough lateral surfaces.
facts.quote: The prefrontals are large triangular plates which overhang the orbits, with rugose lateral surfaces

facts.statement: The squamosal bone possessed five distinct projections.
facts.quote: The squamosal has five projections

facts.statement: The front part of the lower jaw is preserved, showing up to the first eight teeth.
facts.quote: The anterior parts of the dentary are preserved, up to the first eight teeth

facts.statement: Only the centrum of the atlas vertebra is preserved, featuring a crescent shape and a rounded front surface.
facts.quote: The centrum of the atlas vertebra is the only part preserved, and has a crescent shape and rounded anterior surface

facts.statement: The tail vertebrae had prominent facets for haemal arches and tall, plate-like neural spines.
facts.quote: The caudal vertebrae have pronounced facets for the haemal arches, and tall plate-like neural spines

facts.statement: Five dermal scutes found near the tail vertebrae likely belonged to the tail region.
facts.quote: Five dermal scutes were found close to the caudal vertebrae, indicating that they are probably from the tail

facts.statement: The two largest scutes were rectangular with articulatory processes, suggesting they overlapped and linked together.
facts.quote: The two largest are rectangular and have articulatory processes, indicating that they would have overlapped and linked together

facts.statement: Polonosuchus is classified as a distinct genus within the Rauisuchia.
facts.quote: taxon: Polonosuchus

facts.statement: Polonosuchus belongs to the family Rauisuchidae.
facts.quote: familia: Rauisuchidae

facts.statement: Polonosuchus is classified in the order Rauisuchia.
facts.quote: ordo: Rauisuchia

facts.statement: Polonosuchus falls within the unranked group Crurotarsi.
facts.quote: unranked_ordo: Crurotarsi

facts.statement: It is debated whether Polonosuchus is distinct enough from Teratosaurus suevicus, as it is still considered closely related to that species.
facts.quote: However, it is still considered closely related to the remaining Teratosaurus species, Teratosaurus suevicus

facts.statement: Polonosuchus differs from Teratosaurus in having a rostromedial foramen on the medial maxilla surface and replacement tooth foramina arranged in a straight line rather than a groove.
facts.quote: In Polonosuchus, the rostromedial foramen is on the medial surface of the maxilla, and the foramina for replacement teeth are not connected by a dental groove but are set together in a straight line, unlike in Teratosaurus

facts.statement: Polonosuchus had a larger first tooth socket, smaller overall maxillae (165 mm vs 245 mm), and a unique ridge between the palatal process and tooth sockets not found in Teratosaurus.
facts.quote: It also had a larger first dental alveolus than Teratosaurus, no different in size from alveoli 2-4, smaller overall maxillae (165 mm as opposed to 245 mm), and a large ridge between the palatal process and the dental alveoli which is not present in Teratosaurus at all

facts.statement: Polonosuchus lived between 233.6 and 227.3 million years ago during the Carnian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (233.6 to 227.3 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The maxillae were tall and laterally compressed, forming most of the borders of the antorbital fenestra.
rejected.quote: The maxillae are tall and laterally compressed, forming most of the borders of the antorbital fenestra
